title: ר' חלפתא איש כפר חנניה
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: R. Chalafta of Kefar Chananyah, mentioned in chapter 3 of Avot; see R. Chalafta above. End of HaPoalim, 94a: Abba Chalafta says in R. Meir's name. Kefar Chananyah apparently is Kefar Chana, as appears in chapter 9 of Sheviit. He said, “I asked Shimon ben Chananyah, who asked R. Chananyah ben Teradyon's son, and he said, etc.; his daughter says, etc. When these words were stated before R. Yehudah ben Bava, he said, ‘His daughter spoke well’”: Tosefta Kelim, chapter 4. See Beruryah above. Gelilot Eretz Yisrael: at Kefar Anan, R. Chalafta of Kefar Chananyah is buried, with a monument and a sandiyon tree, and there are two graves of R. Chalafta's sons, R. Yosi and R. Shimon. See R. Yaakov of Kefar Chananyah. Perhaps Gelilot Eretz Yisrael has an error [source ש״ס] and should read Kefar Chanan or Chananyah; R. Yosi and R. Shimon are R. Chalafta's sons, as in the preceding entry.
